sections.content:
Interesting! When I clicked the dot at (37,18):
- The dot at (37,18) turned into a 2x2 magenta (M) square at (36-37, 17-18)!
- The dot at (41,16) disappeared (S→B).
So, clicking a dot "activates" it: the dot becomes a 2x2 colored square (magenta), and the next dot in the chain disappears? Or: the dot at (37,18) became a magenta square, and the dot at (41,16) was consumed.
Hmm, wait. Let me think. The HUD palette has S, M, p, Y (sky, magenta, purple, yellow). The dots were sky (S). When I clicked the dot at (37,18), it turned into a 2x2 magenta (M) square, and the dot at (41,16) (the next dot in the lower-left direction) disappeared.
Maybe the mechanic is this: the dots form a chain/path. When you click a dot, it "ignites" and turns into a colored square (the next color in the palette?), and the adjacent dot gets consumed...
Or: this is a "chain reaction" game. Each dot is a node. When you click a node, it turns into a 2x2 square of a specific color, and the next node in the sequence disappears (or the previous one). The goal might be to light up all the dots, or to make the flower change color.
Let me look at the dot layout again:
(37,18), (37,41), (40,37), (41,16), (54,49), (55,14), (56,47), (57,16).
Left side: (41,16), (37,18), (55,14), (57,16) — hmm.
Right side: (37,41), (40,37), (54,49), (56,47).
Maybe the dots form two "arms" extending downward from the flower: the left arm is (37,18) → (41,16) → (55,14) → (57,16)? And the right arm is (37,41) → (40,37) → (56,47) → (54,49)?
Actually, when I clicked (37,18), it became magenta and (41,16) disappeared. So the chain might proceed from (37,18) to (41,16): clicking a dot turns it into a square, and the next dot in the chain is consumed/removed? That's strange.
Or, the dots might be "fuel": each click converts one dot into a colored square, and the color cycles through the palette S→M→p→Y? The first click produced M (magenta). Hmm, but the dot was S (sky). The palette order in the HUD: S, M, p, Y.
Wait — maybe the color of the square produced depends on the position in the chain, or on the "order" of clicks. The first click produced M.
Let me click another dot and observe. Click (37,41) (the right-side counterpart).
